newsitem.title: USA: Calif developer refuses to answer SEC bond queries.
newsitem.headline: Calif developer refuses to answer SEC bond queries.

text.p: A former developer subpoenaed by the Securities and Exchange Commission as part of its probe of Nevada County, Calif. bonds has refused to answer the SEC's queries, his attorney said on Monday.

G. Michael Montross, who is being held in a San Mateo County jail pending a December preliminary hearing on charges of California securities violations, was subpoenaed by the SEC to answer questions about the Nevada County bonds.
David Packard, an attorney for Montross, said his client met with the SEC late last week, but as expected, declined to to answer the SEC's questions about the Nevada County deal.
"Montross asserted his Fifth Amendment privilege not to incriminate himself," Packard said.
SEC officials in San Francisco were not immediately available to comment. They have refused comment in the past.

More than two years ago, the San Mateo County District Attorney's office filed 93 counts of state securities violations against Montross related to two failed land developments, including one in Nevada County.
After more than two years on the run, Montross was taken into custody in June. He has pleaded not guilty to all of the San Mateo County charges.
The charges brought by the district attorney did not specifically involve the Nevada County bonds. But the Nevada County bonds are the subject of an SEC investigation.

Packard said he believes Montross could be a target in the SEC bond probe, which has focused on the county, underwriter First California Capital Markets Group Inc and other bond professionals involved in the deal.
